shelves.title: Hobby Tips
shelves.intro: The stuff I wish someone had told me when I picked up a brush in 2023. Cheap fixes first, tradeoffs explained, and no pretending every mini has to be a display piece.

shelves.title: SDCC Field Guide
shelves.intro: What I've learned from five trips to San Diego Comic-Con, turned into a plan a first-timer can actually follow. Personal experience, not official Comic-Con policy: current-year rules always get checked against comic-con.org.

your-first-mini.title: Your first mini: the minimum setup that actually matters
your-first-mini.dek: Two brushes, a handful of paints, primer, water, paper towel and decent light. Everything else can wait.

your-first-10-minis.title: Your first 10 minis: a better beginner roadmap
your-first-10-minis.dek: Just get started. Give each early mini one job, don't be precious about them, and let photos show you the progress.

tabletop-first-contrast.title: Tabletop-first painting: contrast beats perfect blends
tabletop-first-contrast.dek: Paint for the distance the mini will actually be seen from. Readable beats smooth.

plan-the-palette.title: Plan the palette before you paint
plan-the-palette.dek: Five minutes lining up base, mid and highlight for every color saves an hour of guessing on the mini.

next-10-paints.title: The next 10 paints to buy after a starter set
next-10-paints.dek: Buy the colors that remove friction from what you paint often, not the ones that look fun on the rack.

metallic-drybrushing.title: Metallic drybrushing that looks like metal, not silver dust
metallic-drybrushing.dek: Almost-dry brush, light strokes, a blue-grey underlayer, and metallics saved for last.

beginner-osl.title: Beginner OSL: make the light source read before you chase smoothness
beginner-osl.dek: The light has to be brighter than what it lights, and it has to fade with distance. Glow paint alone won't do it.

basing-as-composition.title: Basing as composition, not decoration
basing-as-composition.dek: A good base supports the pose, tells a bit of the story, and points the eye at the face. Then it gets out of the way.

budget-mini-photography.title: Budget mini photography: make the paint job look like it does in person
budget-mini-photography.dek: Your minis don't suck, your lighting does. Construction paper, a daylight bulb, a mug and a timer fix most of it.

golden-angle.title: Every mini has a golden angle
golden-angle.dek: Sculptors design a pose to read from one direction. Rotate, shoot a few, and find it.

old-dslr-for-minis.title: Shooting minis on an old DSLR (and when better gear actually helps)
old-dslr-for-minis.dek: My 2013 Canon Rebel and its kit lens, the settings card I started with, and what I'd change now: better light instead of flash.

velvet-backdrop.title: Foam vs. velvet: the cheapest photo upgrade I've made
velvet-backdrop.dek: Same mini, same light. Black velvet eats stray light so the background goes truly black and the paint does the work.

batch-priming.title: Priming in batches with a rattlecan
batch-priming.dek: Cheap hardware-store primer, the right color for the game, and a whole army done in one session so future you can just paint.

magnetize-200-minis.title: How I magnetized about 200 minis in about 20 minutes
magnetize-200-minis.dek: A baking sheet, parchment paper, hot glue and 6x2mm magnets. The station is what makes it fast.

marvel-united-storage.title: How I store a whole Marvel United collection
marvel-united-storage.dek: Grab-and-go core boxes, one wooden case for every expansion card, and numbered boxes that tell you where every mini lives.

brush-organization.title: Brush organization without gadgets
brush-organization.dek: Masking tape stripes on the handle. Less magic, more dead simple.

hobby-slump.title: Hobby slump or setup problem? Four ways to restart momentum
hobby-slump.dek: Sometimes it's motivation. More often the paints are buried and the next step is fuzzy. Make starting smaller.

zenithal-priming.title: Quick zenithal priming with two rattlecans
zenithal-priming.dek: Black first, then a couple of white swipes from above. Free contrast before you open a paint pot.

easing-into-the-airbrush.title: Easing into the airbrush (there's no rush)
easing-into-the-airbrush.dek: I waited a long time before picking one up. What I use it for now, and the habits that helped.
